citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- the SAME git-tracked vector the autocorrelation, PACF, AR, Ljung-Box and ADF cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg_poz_s002r02) -> PhysioAnalysis::kpssTest(lag=10): demean, cumulatively sum the residuals to S_t, and eta = N^-2 sum S_t^2 / lrv with lrv a Bartlett (Newey-West) long-run variance (truncation lag 10). The reference re-computes eta with statsmodels.tsa.stattools.kpss(regression=c) and also runs adfTest/adfuller for the confirmatory pair, via reticulate. Deterministic.
note: The root is the POz channel numeric vector (shared with the autocorrelation, PACF, AR, Ljung-Box and ADF cases). The KPSS test is the COMPLEMENT of the ADF test: KPSS null = stationarity (a small statistic fails to reject stationarity), ADF null = unit root (a large-negative statistic rejects it). kpssTest is a NEW op completing the ADF/KPSS confirmatory pair. Its STATISTIC reproduces statsmodels.tsa.stattools.kpss(regression=c) BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| ~7e-16) -- an exact deterministic quantity given the truncation lag. HONEST caveat (as for ADF): only the statistic is bit-exact; the KPSS critical values and p-value come from the reference tables (an approximation), so this op does NOT compute them -- the decision compares against statsmodels tabulated 5% critical value. Finding: KPSS eta=0.20 is below the 5% critical value (0.463), so it FAILS to reject stationarity, and this AGREES with the ADF test (which rejects the unit root): the two complementary tests concur the eyes-closed EEG segment is stationary -- the strongest form of the stationarity conclusion (ADF and KPSS can disagree, signalling near-unit-root / fractional integration; here they do not).
